name: Mazdutide
used_for: Once-weekly glucagon and GLP-1 receptor dual agonist discovered by Eli Lilly and developed in China by Innovent. According to a published review (Drugs, 2025), it was approved in China in June 2025 for long-term weight management and in September 2025 for glycemic control in adults with type 2 diabetes. It has no FDA approval: no Drugs@FDA or DailyMed product exists, and the only US-registered trials found were Lilly phase 2 studies (obesity, alcohol use disorder). Published phase 3 data come from Chinese adults.

entries.text: Once-weekly subcutaneous mazdutide 4 mg or 6 mg for 48 weeks.
entries.population: Chinese adults with overweight or obesity (GLORY-1, phase 3)

entries.text: Once-weekly subcutaneous mazdutide 9 mg for 60 weeks.
entries.population: Chinese adults with obesity, BMI 30 or higher (GLORY-2, phase 3)

entries.text: Once-weekly subcutaneous mazdutide with escalation to 3/6 mg, 10 mg or 16 mg for 48 weeks (starting at 1.5 mg).
entries.population: US adults with obesity or overweight (Lilly phase 2, as registered)

administration_guidance.text: In the GLORY-2 trial, mazdutide was given once weekly by subcutaneous administration alongside a reduced-calorie diet and increased physical activity. Mazdutide is investigational and has no label guidance on timing, meals, or storage.
administration_guidance.label: research

administration_guidance.text: An educational peptide site says mazdutide injections can be given regardless of meal timing, that an empty stomach or a light meal may reduce discomfort if GI effects occur, that unreconstituted product is kept at 2 to 8 C away from light and not frozen, and that a reconstituted vial is typically used within 14 to 28 days per its labeling. Mazdutide is unapproved in the US, so this is not label guidance.
administration_guidance.label: internet

side_effects.text: In GLORY-2 (Chinese adults with obesity), the most common adverse events were vomiting (53.1% vs 1.3% with placebo), nausea (46.9% vs 3.2%), and diarrhea (39.4% vs 6.5%), mostly mild to moderate. Discontinuation due to adverse events was 2.9% with mazdutide vs 0% with placebo.
side_effects.label: research

side_effects.text: In GLORY-1, the most frequent adverse events were gastrointestinal and mostly mild to moderate, and adverse events led to discontinuation in 0.5% to 1.5% of mazdutide recipients and 1.0% of those on placebo.
side_effects.label: research

internet_claims.claim: Superpower, a health testing company, says mazdutide showed about 13 percent placebo-subtracted weight loss at 6 mg in Chinese trials, but that safety data come only from Chinese trials of 32 weeks or less, and that it has no legal pathway for US use.
FormBlends says mazdutide is not FDA-approved or legally available in US pharmacies, cautions that online vendors' product quality is unverifiable, and points US readers to approved drugs.

Peptide Local, an information site, says mazdutide is approved in China but not by the FDA, that a Chinese approval does not carry over to other countries, and cites an FDA warning letter about a seller's mazdutide listing.

research.summary: GLORY-1: phase 3, 48-week trial of mazdutide 4 mg or 6 mg versus placebo in 610 Chinese adults with overweight or obesity (N Engl J Med; NCT05607680).
research.finding: Week 48 weight change was -11.0% (4 mg) and -14.0% (6 mg) versus +0.3% with placebo. Gastrointestinal events were most common; 0.5 to 1.5% stopped for adverse events. Results apply to Chinese adults.

research.summary: GLORY-2: phase 3, 60-week trial of mazdutide 9 mg versus placebo in 461 Chinese adults with obesity (JAMA; NCT06164873).
research.finding: Weight change was -16.65% versus -1.50% with placebo. Vomiting (53%), nausea (47%) and diarrhea (39%) were common; 2.9% stopped treatment.

research.summary: 28-week phase 3 trial of mazdutide 4 or 6 mg versus dulaglutide 1.5 mg in 731 Chinese adults with type 2 diabetes (Nature; NCT05606913).
research.finding: HbA1c fell more than with dulaglutide (-0.24 and -0.30 points difference) and weight fell more. Gastrointestinal side effects were more frequent than with dulaglutide.

research.summary: 24-week phase 3 trial of mazdutide monotherapy versus placebo in 320 Chinese adults with type 2 diabetes (Nature; NCT05628311).
research.finding: HbA1c fell 1.57 (4 mg) and 2.15 (6 mg) points versus 0.14 with placebo; weight fell 5.6 to 7.8% versus 1.3%. Short trial, Chinese participants only.

research.summary: Lilly phase 2 US trial of mazdutide versus placebo for 48 weeks in 179 adults with obesity or overweight.
research.finding: Posted results show week 32 weight change of -7.3% (3/6 mg), -15.6% (10 mg) and -18.1% (16 mg) versus -0.85% with placebo. Only the posted primary outcome table was reviewed; a peer-reviewed paper was not found.

research.summary: Lilly phase 2 US proof-of-concept trial of mazdutide versus placebo in 308 people with alcohol use disorder.
research.finding: Registered as completed in March 2026; no results were posted when reviewed, so there is no verified finding.

research.summary: FDA warning letter dated 31 March 2026 to Prime Sciences.
research.finding: The letter lists mazdutide, among other products, as an unapproved new drug offered for sale for human use despite laboratory-research-only labeling.

research.summary: FDA warning letter dated 10 December 2024 to Xcel Research LLC.
research.finding: The letter lists mazdutide, among other peptides, as an unapproved new drug sold with research-use-only labels.
